data_section_full_text:
The sample begins with annual random samples of 1,000 Compustat firms
drawn each year during the period 1972–1998, where 1972 is the first year
that quarterly earnings announcement data are available on Compustat. A
firm is included in a given year only if it has four quarterly earnings announcement dates available. This results in a potential sample of 108,000
firm-quarter observations over the twenty-seven years. <sup>1</sup> We next impose a
data availability criterion necessary to compute the abnormal volume and
return metrics. Specifically, to compute out-of-sample estimates of normal
volume and volatility, a firm-quarter observation is excluded if there is missing daily volume or return data in the two trading years surrounding the
earnings announcement, i.e., during the periods t - 345 to t - 20 and t + 20
to t + 345. <sup>2</sup> This results in deletion of 3,340 firm-quarters. We next impose two criteria to screen extreme observations. In particular, we exclude
2,066 firm-quarters with negative equity book values and 1,029 firm-quarters
with core earnings-to-price in the top and bottom 0.5% of each quarter,

1 We also conducted separate analyses on the largest one thousand firms in Compustat in
each sample quarter, where size is defined as market value of equity. Empirical inferences from
unreported findings are qualitatively similar to those reported in the paper.

2 For an observation to be included in the sample we require at least 100 days of volume and
return data before the earnings announcement, i.e., in the period, t - 345 to t - 20, and 100
observations after the earnings announcement, i.e., in the period t + 20 to t + 345. To avoid
contamination from other earnings announcements, the non-announcement period excludes
the 20 trading days surrounding those announcements.

where core earnings is defined as in Collins, Maydew, and Weiss [1997] as
earnings before extraordinary items, discontinued operations, and special
items. Finally, we exclude an additional 8,952 firm-quarters with missing
